issues.legal_issue: A contract for the sale of immovable property was concluded when the parties made reciprocal promises to sell and buy without making formation dependent on the property remaining unrequisitioned.
material_facts: The agreement stated that the seller agreed to sell and the purchasers agreed to purchase the premises.
The agreement separately provided for execution of a sale deed after the premises were vacated by the income-tax authorities.
Neither party disputed that an agreement had been formed.
issues.conclusion: A concluded contract existed, and the seller and purchasers became bound by their respective promises from the inception of the agreement.
issues.legal_principle: The agreement must be read as a whole. Its promise to sell and purchase, together with the provision requiring the seller to execute a sale deed, showed a concluded contract; it was not made subject to the property remaining unrequisitioned. The Court relied on the agreement’s clauses 1 and 5 and cited no earlier case for this point.

predicates.sale_contract_dispute: A dispute arose over an agreement for the sale of immovable property.
predicates.reciprocal_sale_promises: The agreement contained promises by the seller to sell and by the purchasers to buy the property.
predicates.contract_formation_subject_to_nonrequisi: The agreement made the existence of the contract dependent on the property not being requisitioned.

issues.definition: When a sale-contract dispute involves reciprocal promises and contract formation is not dependent on non-requisition, a concluded contract exists.

issues.legal_issue: Requisition of the property did not end or suspend the seller’s obligation to sell where the agreement did not make that obligation conditional on non-requisition.
material_facts: The agreement required the seller to refund the earnest money with interest if the property was requisitioned before registration of the sale deed.
The agreement did not state that the seller’s obligation to sell was conditional on non-requisition or that requisition ended the contract.
The property was requisitioned before execution of the sale deed, and the purchasers continued to request completion.
issues.conclusion: Non-requisition was not a condition precedent to the seller’s obligation to sell, and requisition did not terminate that obligation.
issues.legal_principle: The Court construed the agreement’s language and commercial context. It found no express wording making the seller’s obligation conditional on non-requisition or ending the contract upon requisition; the refund term was consistent with a right of the purchasers to rescind. No earlier case was relied on for this interpretation.

predicates.sale_contract_dispute: A dispute arose over an agreement for the sale of immovable property.
predicates.property_requisitioned_before_transfer: The property was requisitioned before the agreed transfer was completed.
predicates.agreement_makes_seller_obligation_condit: The agreement states that the seller’s obligation to sell depends on the property not being requisitioned.

issues.definition: When property is requisitioned before transfer under a sale agreement that does not condition the seller’s obligation on non-requisition, the seller’s obligation to sell survives.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser may unilaterally waive a contractual condition that exists exclusively for the purchaser’s benefit and imposes no liability on the purchaser.
material_facts: The requisition clause gave the purchasers the right to demand return of the earnest money with interest if the property was requisitioned.
The clause imposed a refund obligation on the seller but no corresponding liability on the purchasers.
The purchasers chose to insist on the sale rather than rescind and repeatedly sought execution of the sale deed.
issues.conclusion: The purchasers could unilaterally waive the condition and insist on performance of the seller’s obligation.
issues.legal_principle: A contractual stipulation may be waived unilaterally by the party for whose exclusive benefit it was made, provided it creates no liability against that party. The Court distinguished Dalsukh M. Pancholi v. The Guarantee Life and Employment Insurance Co. Ltd., AIR 1947 PC 182, where the stipulation was not exclusively for the purchaser’s benefit, and also referred to Hawksley v. Outram, [1892] 3 Ch. 259, and Morrell v. Studd and Millington, [1913] 2 Ch. 648.

rule.if: sale_contract_dispute and condition_for_one_party_only and not condition_imposes_liability_on_beneficiary and beneficiary_elects_performance

predicates.sale_contract_dispute: A dispute arose over an agreement for the sale of immovable property.
predicates.condition_for_one_party_only: The contractual condition was made exclusively for the benefit of one contracting party.
predicates.condition_imposes_liability_on_beneficia: The condition imposes a liability on the party for whose benefit it was made.
predicates.beneficiary_elects_performance: The party benefiting from the condition chooses to proceed with the contract rather than exercise the option the condition provides.

issues.definition: A party may unilaterally waive an exclusively beneficial condition that imposes no liability on that party by choosing to proceed with the contract.

issues.legal_issue: Delay in seeking specific performance does not bar relief when the claimant has not waived the remedy and the delay has not placed the other party at an unfair disadvantage.
material_facts: The purchasers waited while an appeal against the requisition order was pending, reasonably hoping the order would be set aside.
After the appeal was dismissed, the purchasers repeatedly pressed for execution of the sale deed and demonstrated readiness to pay the consideration.
The seller did not plead or prove that delay had caused disadvantage, and the evidence did not show abandonment of the purchasers’ rights.
issues.conclusion: The purchasers’ delay did not disentitle them to specific performance.
issues.legal_principle: Under Lindsay Petroleum Co. v. Hurd, L.R. 5 P.C. 221 at 239, delay and lapse of time are material where a party’s conduct is equivalent to waiver or has put the other party in a situation in which it would be unreasonable to grant the remedy. The Court found neither waiver nor disadvantage here.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and claimant_waited_for_related_appeal and claimant_kept_asserting_rights and not opponent_disadvantage_shown

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The proceeding seeks specific performance of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.claimant_waited_for_related_appeal: The claimant waited for the outcome of an appeal concerning an obstacle to completion of the transaction.
predicates.claimant_kept_asserting_rights: The claimant continued to demand performance and did not abandon the contractual claim.
predicates.opponent_disadvantage_shown: The opposing party showed that delay placed it at an unfair disadvantage.

issues.definition: In a specific-performance suit, waiting for a related appeal does not bar relief when the claimant continues to assert the right and no unfair disadvantage to the opponent is shown.
